text:
Sidney Crosby's future is the biggest question in Pittsburgh, and this week it got loud. His agent spoke publicly about it, Crosby addressed it with a contract decision looming, and Daily Faceoff ran the headline nobody in Pittsburgh wanted to read: "Say it ain't Sid: are we finally seeing Crosby's decline?"

Our numbers say the scoring has slipped more than the player. Crosby has 15 points in 24 games, five in his last ten, and his points per 60 sit below the bottom of our likely range for him. But he is still creating: about 1.04 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, slightly up on last season, and the Penguins' on-ice chances in his last ten are above his usual. He has six goals on 8.1 expected, and Pittsburgh has scored 6.5 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there. That reads as bad luck on a team that lost eight of those ten, not a 39-year-old who has stopped getting to the net.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season. The passing is still there; what happens next in Pittsburgh is the bigger question.
